title: Insert Greatest Common Divisors in Linked List
summary: For every pair of neighboring original nodes, insert one new node between them.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–5000 nodes with values in [1,1000]. Serialize the final next chain as values. The wrapper also checks original identities at alternating positions and fresh inserted nodes between them.
contractDetails.output-checking: Build ListNode objects, invoke the callable, and verify alternating original and fresh inserted identities, preserved original values, bounded length, and a null tail. Then compare the full value sequence.

statement: For every pair of neighboring original nodes, insert one new node between them. Its value is the greatest common divisor of their values. Return the head of the modified list. Keep the original nodes, values, and relative order.

examples.explanation: The gaps receive gcd values 2 and 5.
One original node has no gaps.
Equal values still represent different original and inserted node objects.

constraints: 1–5000 nodes with values in [1,1000]. Serialize the final next chain as values. The wrapper also checks original identities at alternating positions and fresh inserted nodes between them.
hints: Conceptual: Every original gap needs its own new node.
Directional: Compute the divisor from the two original nodes at the gap.
Implementation: Save the next original node, insert a fresh node pointing to it, and advance to that original node rather than the inserted one.
complexityAnalysis: O(n log V) time for Euclid’s algorithm and O(1) auxiliary solution space, excluding the n−1 new nodes. V is the largest value.
